ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p38/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p38/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p38/r3.claim: Moses was a messenger and Aaron a prophet; both are called messengers by addressing the pair through its dominant member (ʿalā sabīl al-taghlīb).
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p38/r3.anchor: The status of Moses (sws) was that of a messenger

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p38/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p38/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p38/r4.claim: The pair are called messengers by reference to the dominant member; the release demand is linked to Moses's intended destination for the Israelites and to 7:104–105.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p38/r4.anchor: both are called messengers because it is like

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p38/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p38/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p38/r5.claim: The wording “let the Israelites go with us” was explained at 7:104–105, where Islahi discusses where Moses intended to take them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p38/r5.anchor: The words “so let the Israelites go with us”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p39/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p39/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p39/r1.claim: Islahi rejects the view that Moses was merely a nationalist leader whose activity was a freedom movement.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p39/r1.anchor: was a nationalist leader and his endeavours were more of a movement for freedom

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p39/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p39/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p39/r2.claim: Āyah means an argument or reason regardless of number; 7:105 likewise calls Moses's proof a clear argument, and the early miracles are discussed elsewhere.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p39/r2.anchor: means argument and reason regardless of number

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p39/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p39/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p39/r3.claim: The greeting expresses prophetic sincerity and sympathy as instructed at 20:44, while subtly warning Pharaoh that peace requires accepting guidance or facing the consequences.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p39/r3.anchor: which is a hallmark of the preaching of prophets

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p39/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p39/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p39/r4.claim: The greeting is also a subtle warning: after guidance has arrived, the path to peace is the straight path, or consequences follow.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p39/r4.anchor: the way to peace is to adopt the straight path

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r3.claim: Calling Pharaoh's God his Lord diminishes Pharaoh and declares him a created, owned subject; the mission also demands Israel's release from forced labor, abuse, and killing of their sons.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r3.anchor: وخاطباه بقولهما ربك تحقيرا له وإعلاما أنه مربوب مملوك إذ كان هو يدعي الربوبية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r4.claim: The messengers' message to Pharaoh comprises belief in God and release of the Israelites; other verses also mention the call to faith.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r4.anchor: وقد ذكر في غير هذه الآية دعاؤه إلى الإيمان فجملة ما دعا إليه فرعون الإيمان وإرسال بني إسرائيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r5.claim: The staff and hand are the signs; since both shared the mission, the sign is attributed to both although one messenger produced it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r5.anchor: والآية التي أحالا عليها هي العصا واليد، ولما كانا مشتركين في الرسالة صح نسبة المجيء بالآية إليهما وإن كانت صادرة من أحدهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes the singular sign as a generic proof that substantiates the preceding claim of messengership; he cites comparable Qur'anic formulations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r6.anchor: لأن دعوى الرسالة لا تثبت إلا ببينتها التي هي المجيء بالآية، وإنما وحد بآية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r7.claim: One view identifies the sign as the hand; another identifies it as the staff, either of which testifies to their mission.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p338/r7.anchor: وقيل: الآية اليد. وقيل: العصا، والمعنى بآية تشهد لنا بأنا رسولا ربك

QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r3.claim: Israel’s suffering under Pharaoh lasted a long time, but God eventually rescued them; His pattern is to give an oppressor rein before seizing him painfully.
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r3.anchor: طال البلاء ببني إسرائيل من جهة فرعون

QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r7.claim: Only a heart illuminated by gnosis follows guidance; one covered by ignorance cannot hear it.
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r7.anchor: إنما يتبع الهدى من كحل قلبه بنور العرفان

QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r8.claim: Every prophet warns his people of punishment for abandoning God’s command and promises reward for keeping it.
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r8.anchor: ما بعث الله نبيا إلا وقد أنذر قومه بالعذاب على ترك الأمر

QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r9.claim: The details of deferred punishment and deferred reward remain unknown to those awaiting them.
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r9.anchor: فمؤجله لا يوقف على تفصيله الأعداء وكذلك مؤجل الثواب

QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r10.claim: Immediate punishments take many forms and are directed according to a person’s station; the kind and degree of punishment reflect what is due.
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r10.anchor: وأما معجل العقوبة فأنواع ، وعلى حسبت مقام المرء

QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r11.claim: Hardness of heart, obstruction in obedience, and losses of wealth or life are forms of immediate punishment.
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r11.anchor: وقسوة القلب نوع عقوبة ، وما يتداخل الطاعة نوع عقوبة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r2.claim: The messengers ask Pharaoh to release Israel from his service and not exhaust them with hard labor.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r2.anchor: أي: خل عنهم وأطلقهم من أعمالك، {ولا تعذبهم} لا تتعبهم في العمل. وكان فرعون يستعملهم في الأعمال الشاقة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r3.claim: Peace for whoever follows guidance means safety from God's punishment for whoever submits, not a greeting.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r3.anchor: ليس المراد منه التحية، إنما معناه سلم من عذاب الله من أسلم.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r1.claim: The sign from Pharaoh's Lord is a great proof, including the staff and hand, that obliges him to accept the messengers' claim and submit to guidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r1.anchor: موجبة لقبول ما ادعيناه من العصا واليد وغيرهما

BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r2.claim: Repeating the address intensifies Pharaoh's reproach for claiming lordship and denying God's favor; peace is specifically his if he accepts guidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r2.anchor: وفي تكرير مخاطبته بذلك تأكيد لتبكيته في ادعاء الربوبية

BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r3.claim: Peace belongs generally to everyone who follows guidance; refusal leaves Pharaoh exposed to destruction and punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r3.anchor: وإذا كان هذا الجنس عليهم كان من المعلوم أن العطب على غيرهم

DURR-FULL:v5p573/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas tells the narrator that eight years were obligatory and Moses would not shorten them; God fulfilled the promised term of ten years.
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r1.anchor: فقال: أما كنت تعلم أن ثمانيا واجبة لم يكن موسى لينتقص منها وتعلم أن الله تعالى كان قاضيا عن موسى عدته

DURR-FULL:v5p573/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r2.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r2.claim: The story says Moses feared Pharaoh over the killing, had a speech impediment, and asked God for Aaron's support so Aaron could speak for him; God granted this and ordered Aaron to meet him.
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r2.anchor: فشكا إلى ربه ما يتخوف من آل فرعون في القتيل وعقدة لسانه - فإنه كان في لسانه عقدة تمنعه من كثير من الكلام - فسأل ربه أن يعينه بأخيه هارون

DURR-FULL:v5p581/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r1.claim: When entering the homes of People of the Book, one should greet them: peace upon whoever follows guidance.
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r1.anchor: عن قتادة قال: التسليم على أهل الكتاب إذا دخلت عليهم بيوتهم أن تقول: السلام على من اتبع الهدى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r1.claim: Moses and Aaron were to tell Pharaoh they were his messengers, release Israel, and stop their oppression; calling him Pharaoh rather than affirming his claimed lordship belittles him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r1.anchor: أتيا فرعون فأعلماه أنكما رسولاي إليه وعبر بفرعون تحقيرا له إذ كان هو يدعي الربوبية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r2.claim: The request to release Israel supplements the earlier call to faith; Pharaoh’s commission to them differs from the mission to Israel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r2.anchor: وهذه جملة ما دعي إليه فرعون الإيمان وإرسال بني إسرائيل، والظاهر أن رسالته إليه ليست على حد إرساله إلى بني إسرائيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r3.claim: Israel’s oppression consisted of killing their sons, forced service, and humiliation; the signs invoked were the staff and hand.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r3.anchor: وتعذيب بني إسرائيل كان ذبح أولادهم وتسخيرهم وإذلالهم والآية التي أحالا عليها هي العصا واليد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r4.claim: Moses is the one who brought the sign, while the dual wording jointly attributes it to both messengers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r4.anchor: وقالا جئناك والجائي بها موسى تجوزا من حيث كانا مشركين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r5.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r5.claim: One reading makes Peace be upon whoever follows guidance a closing greeting, separated from the preceding statement; it reproaches Pharaoh.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r5.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون آخر كلام وفصله فيقوى أن يكون السلام بمعنى التحية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r7.claim: The narrative omits that the messengers went to Pharaoh and delivered all they were commanded before he asked who their Lord was.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r7.anchor: وفي سرد هذه الآية حذف يدل عليه ظاهر الكلام تقديره فأتياه فلما قالا جميع ما أمرا به قال لهما فرعون

JISHUMI:v7p4672/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r11.claim: The command to release the Israelites means freeing them from captivity and not tormenting them; another explanation specifies slaughtering sons, enslaving men, and sparing women.
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r11.anchor: أي: أطلقهم من اعتقالك ولا تعذبهم، وقيل: بذبح الأبناء، واستعباد الرجال، واستحياء النساء،

JISHUMI:v7p4672/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r12.claim: The sign from God was a proof, identified as the staff and hand; alternatively, the two answered Pharaoh's request for evidence by saying they had brought a sign.
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r12.anchor: قد جئناك بآية بحجة من ربك اليد والعصا، وقيل: كأنه قيل لهما: ما الحجة على ما قلتما؟

JISHUMI:v7p4676/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4676/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4676/r1.claim: Moses and Aaron showed Pharaoh miracles; the duty to believe follows from miracles, as their statement that they brought a sign indicates.
JISHUMI:v7p4676/r1.anchor: وتدل على أنه أظهر عنده المعجزات، وأن التصديق إنما يجب عند المعجزات لذلك قال: (جئناك بآية).

QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r1.claim: The account omits an action: the two went to Pharaoh and then said the quoted message to him.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r1.anchor: في الكلام حذف، والمعنى: فأتياه فقالا له ذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r2.claim: The command to release the Israelites means to let them go free; they endured severe forced labor and abuse, including the killing of sons and enslavement of women.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r2.anchor: أي خل عنهم. { ولا تعذبهم } أي بالسخرة والتعب في العمل، وكان بنو إسرائيل عند فرعون في عذاب شديد

QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r3.claim: Pharaoh made the Israelites kill sons and spare women, and imposed unbearable work making clay, bricks, and cities.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r3.anchor: يذبح أبناءهم، ويستحيي نساءهم، ويكلفهم من العمل في الطين واللبن وبناء المدائن ما لا يطيقونه.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r4.claim: The sign brought by Moses was the staff and the hand.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد العصا واليد.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r5.claim: In another account, Pharaoh asked what the sign was; Moses drew out his hand, which shone like the sun and outshone it, astonishing Pharaoh.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r5.anchor: فأدخل يده في جيب قميصه، ثم أخرجها بيضاء لها شعاع مثل شعاع الشمس، غلب نورها على نور الشمس فعجب منها.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r6.claim: In this account Pharaoh did not see the staff until the day of the festival.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r6.anchor: ولم يره العصا إلا يوم الزينة.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r7.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r7.claim: “Peace upon whoever follows guidance” promises safety from God's displeasure and punishment; it is not a greeting because no meeting is beginning.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج: أي من اتبع الهدى سلم من سخط الله عز وجل وعذابه. قال: وليس بتحية، والدليل على ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r8.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r8.claim: “Peace upon those who follow guidance” means the same whether expressed with على or لِـ.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r8.anchor: الفراء: السلام على من اتبع الهدى ولمن اتبع الهدى سواء.

ZAJJAJ:v3p358/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p358/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p358/r3.claim: ‘Peace be on whoever follows guidance’ is not a greeting; it means the follower of guidance is safe from God’s punishment and anger, since this is not an opening encounter.
ZAJJAJ:v3p358/r3.anchor: ليس يعنى به التحية، وإنما معناه أن من اتبع الهدى سلم من عذاب الله وسخطه

ZAJJAJ:v3p358/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p358/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p358/r4.claim: The text omits ‘they said to him’ after ‘they went to him’ because context makes it clear; Pharaoh’s next question proves that they spoke to him.
ZAJJAJ:v3p358/r4.anchor: لأن الكلام قد دل على ذلك فاستغنى عنه أن يقال فيه فأتياه فقالا،

TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r2.claim: God sent Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh to tell him that they were messengers from his Creator, free the Children of Israel from enslavement, and stop their harsh forced labor.
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r2.anchor: أي أرسلنا إليك خالقك بما ندعوا إليه { فأرسل معنا بني إسرائيل }

THALABI:v6p246/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p246/r1.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ الرازي
THALABI:v6p246/r1.claim: Yahya ibn Muʿadh marvels at God's gentleness toward someone who claims to be a god, asking how much gentler He is toward someone who affirms God as God.
THALABI:v6p246/r1.anchor: سمعت يحيى بن معاذ الرازي يقول- وقرأ هذه الآية-: هذا رفقك بمن يقول: أنا الإله، فكيف رفقك بمن يقول: أنت الإله؟

THALABI:v6p246/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p246/r2.speaker: أبو القاسم الحسين
THALABI:v6p246/r2.claim: Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn extends the saying: God's gentleness reaches even opponents, enemies, those who insult Him, associate partners, stray, sin, persist, and act proudly; how much more those who love, affirm, confess, repent, or ask forgiveness.
THALABI:v6p246/r2.anchor: فقلت: هذا رفقك بمن ينافيك فكيف رفقك بمن يصافيك؟ هذا رفقك بمن يعاديك فكيف رفقك بمن يواليك؟ هذا رفقك بمن يسبك فكيف رفقك بمن يحبك؟

THALABI:v6p246/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p246/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p246/r7.claim: The instruction not to torment Israel refers to their harsh forced labor under Pharaoh's people, who killed sons, used women, and assigned work beyond their capacity.
THALABI:v6p246/r7.anchor: أي ولا تتعبهم في العمل، وكانت بنو إسرائيل عند آل فرعون في عذاب شديد يقتل أبناءهم ويستخدم نساءهم

THALABI:v6p246/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p246/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p246/r9.claim: Peace upon those who follow guidance means peace upon whoever submits.
THALABI:v6p246/r9.anchor: والسلام على من اتبع الهدى يعني من أسلم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r1.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r1.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the sign brought by Moses as the staff and the hand.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r2.claim: The Prophet used “peace upon whoever follows guidance” as his greeting when writing to polytheists.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p261/r2.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا كتب إلى المشركين كتب: «السلام على من اتبع الهدى» .

STUDYQURAN:20:47/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:47/r1.speaker: Kl
STUDYQURAN:20:47/r1.claim: Moses and Aaron invited Pharaoh to believe in God and release the Children of Israel, whom Pharaoh and his people controlled.
STUDYQURAN:20:47/r1.anchor: Moses and Aaron were inviting Pharaoh to believe in God and to free the children of Israel (Kl) who were under the control of Pharaoh

STUDYQURAN:20:47/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:47/r2.speaker: Kl
STUDYQURAN:20:47/r2.claim: Pharaoh killed Israelite children, forced the people into labor to serve him, and humiliated them.
STUDYQURAN:20:47/r2.anchor: Pharaoh used to kill their children and force them into labor in order to serve him, all the while humiliating them (Kl)

STUDYQURAN:20:47/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:47/r3.speaker: Kl
STUDYQURAN:20:47/r3.claim: The singular “a sign” collectively refers to Moses’ miracles of the staff and the white hand.
STUDYQURAN:20:47/r3.anchor: A sign from your Lord is a collective reference to the miracles of Moses’ staff and his white hand (Kl)

STUDYQURAN:20:47/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:47/r4.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:20:47/r4.claim: Those who believe God’s signs receive peace from God, angels, and believers, bringing safety in this life and the next.
STUDYQURAN:20:47/r4.anchor: whoever believes in God’s signs will have greetings of peace from God, the angels, and the believers

TAB-FULL:v16p78/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p78/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p78/r1.claim: Moses and Aaron demand that Pharaoh release Israel and stop imposing degrading work; they offer a miracle to prove their mission if he doubts them, and declare safety for whoever follows God’s guidance.
TAB-FULL:v16p78/r1.anchor: يقول: والسلامة لمن اتبع هدى الله، وهو بيانه

TAB-FULL:v16p78/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p78/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p78/r2.claim: In this expression, على and لِـ convey the same sense.
TAB-FULL:v16p78/r2.anchor: يقال: السلام على من اتبع الهدى، ولمن اتبع بمعنى واحد

TABATABAI:20:46-47/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r6.claim: After reassuring them, God renews the order and specifies their mission: invite Pharaoh to faith, end Israelite oppression, and release the people.
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r6.anchor: جدد أمرهما بالذهاب إلى فرعون بعد تأمينهما ووعدهما بالحفظ والنصر وبين تمام ما يكلفان به من الرسالة

TABATABAI:20:46-47/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r7.claim: Each command is renewed as the dialogue changes: first Moses is sent, then Aaron joins after Moses' request, and finally the task is specified after their fear is answered.
TABATABAI:20:46-47/r7.anchor: فكلما تحول حال في المحاورة جدد الأمر حسب ما يناسبه وهو قوله أولا

TABATABAI:20:47-48/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r1.claim: Moses and Aaron first declare that they are God's messengers; the greeting of peace then invites Pharaoh to the remaining parts of faith.
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r1.anchor: فقوله { فأتياه فقولا إنا رسولا ربك } تبليغ أنهما رسولا الله،

TABATABAI:20:47-48/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r2.claim: The demand to release the Israelites without torment is a practical command directed to Pharaoh.

TABATABAI:20:47-48/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r3.claim: The sign is a proof establishing their prophethood; its indefinite form leaves the number unspecified while signaling its magnitude, importance, and clarity.
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r3.anchor: استناد إلى حجة تثبت رسالتهما وفي تنكير الآية سكوت عن العدد وإشارة إلى فخامة أمرها

TABATABAI:20:47-48/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r4.claim: The farewell-like greeting completes the message and summarizes its call: safety and happiness belong to those following guidance, in this life and the next.
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r4.anchor: كالتحية للوداع يشار به إلى تمام الرسالة ويبين به خلاصة ما تتضمنه الدعوة الدينية

TABATABAI:20:47-48/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r6.claim: “Come to him” suggests closer contact than “go to him,” diminishing Pharaoh despite the difficulty of approaching Egypt's king and the Copts' god.
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r6.anchor: فقد قيل { فأتياه } ولم يقل إذهبا إليه وإتيان الشيء أقرب مساسا به

TABATABAI:20:47-48/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r7.claim: The wording omits “to him” after “say,” as if Pharaoh merits no special concern.
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r7.anchor: وقيل { فقولا } ولم يقل فقولا له كأنه لا يعتني به،

TABATABAI:20:47-48/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r8.claim: Calling God “your Lord” twice confronts Pharaoh's boast, “I am your highest lord,” with his subordination to a real Lord.
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r8.anchor: وقيل { إنا رسولا ربك } و { بآية من ربك } فقرع سمعه مرتين

TABATABAI:20:47-48/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r9.claim: Neither peace nor the warning of punishment directly addresses Pharaoh, further undercutting his self-importance and matching God's encompassing might.
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r9.anchor: وقيل { والسلام على من اتبع الهدى } ولم يورد بالخطاب إليه، ونظيره قوله { أن العذاب على من كذب وتولى }

TABATABAI:20:47-48/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r10.claim: Despite its directness, the required message is not harsh: truth must reach Pharaoh without flattery or deference to his false power and pride.
TABATABAI:20:47-48/r10.anchor: فإن ذلك حق القول الذي لا مناص من قرعه سمع فرعون من غير تملق ولا احتشام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r1.claim: Some identify the sign Moses brought as the staff, while others identify it as the hand.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r1.anchor: {قد جئناك بآية من ربك} قيل: العصا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r2.claim: Others identify the sign as the hand.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says the singular āya can denote all of Moses’s signs, just as one word can denote a collection of words.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r3.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: (أراد جميع (¬3) آيات موسى، فذكرها بلفظ الواحد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r4.claim: According to ʿAṭāʾ from Ibn Abbas, this is God’s blessing upon whoever follows the message Moses brought.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r4.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: (يريد من الله عز وجل على من اتبع البيان الذي جاء به موسى)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r5.claim: Abū Isḥāq takes salām as safety from God’s punishment and anger for the follower of guidance, not as a greeting.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r5.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (ليس يعني به التحية، وإنما معناه: أن من اتبع الهدى يسلم من عذاب الله وسخطه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r6.claim: The author says ʿAṭāʾ’s interpretation can mean either a greeting or Abū Isḥāq’s sense of safety.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r6.anchor: والذي ذكره عطاء يحتمل التحية ويحتمل ما قاله أبو إسحاق.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r7.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ interprets salām as safety bestowed on the follower of guidance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p412/r7.anchor: وقال الفراء: (يريد والسلامة على من أتبع الهدى

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r7.claim: They ask Pharaoh to release the Israelites and stop enslaving them.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r8.claim: They ask him not to exhaust the Israelites with labor.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r9.claim: The sign is the shining hand and the staff.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r9.anchor: يعني: اليد البيضاء [والعصا] { والسلام على من اتبع الهدى } سلم من أسلم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r10.claim: Whoever submits to the guidance is safe.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r8.claim: The Israelites held among the Egyptians a status like protected-tax communities in Yahya's society.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r8.anchor: {فأتياه فقولا إنا رسولا ربك فأرسل معنا بني إسرائيل ولا تعذبهم} [طه: 47] كان بنو إسرائيل عند القبط بمنزلة أهل الجزية فينا.

QASHANI:20:41-44/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:41-44/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:41-44/r5.claim: Their mission is to tame the soul, stop it enslaving animal powers, and release them to seek divine presence, holy light, and true knowledge instead of sensory pleasures and worldly adornment.
QASHANI:20:41-44/r5.anchor: وأن يرسلها معهما في التوجه إلى الحضرة الإلهية واستفاضة الأنوار الروحية القدسية

QASHANI:20:41-44/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:41-44/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:41-44/r6.claim: The sign is a proof demonstrating that Pharaoh must follow them.
QASHANI:20:41-44/r6.anchor: ببرهان دال على وجوب متابعتك إيانا

QASHANI:20:47/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:47/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:47/r1.claim: Peace means freedom from defects and attachments and the luminous influx of the spiritual world.
QASHANI:20:47/r1.anchor: { والسلام } أي: السلامة من النقائص والنجاة من العلائق والفيض النوري من العالم الروحي

QASHANI:20:47/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:47/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:47/r2.claim: Following guidance means following proof and holding to divine light.
QASHANI:20:47/r2.anchor: { على من اتبع } البرهان وتمسك بالنور الإلهي

SULAMI:v1p445#6/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p445#6/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p445#6/r1.claim: Following guidance is preceded by God's guidance: whoever God first guides follows the path in every state.
SULAMI:v1p445#6/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : اتباع الهدى بسابقة الهدى فمن سبقت له من الله الهداية اتبع الهدى في جميع أحواله .

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p249/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p249/r1.speaker: أبو العباس
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p249/r1.claim: Abu al-ʿAbbās says إن answers a question when unaccompanied by lām, and answers a denier when accompanied by lām.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p249/r1.anchor: فأما الذي ذكر عن أبي العباس من جعله لها جواب سائل ، إذا كانت وحدها . وجواب منكر إذا كان معها اللام .

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p249/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p249/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p249/r2.claim: The author supports إن’s answer function: Moses and Aaron’s message to Pharaoh responds to the implied question of who they are and what brought them.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p249/r2.anchor: فأتياه فإذا قال لكما ما شأنكما ؟ وما جاء بكما ؟ وما تقولان ؟ فقولا : إنا رسول رب العالمين .

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p249/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p249/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p249/r3.claim: إن is fundamentally emphatic and is needed when the hearer suspects the opposite of what is asserted or already believes the contrary.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p249/r3.anchor: وإنما تحتاج إليها إذا كان له ظن في الخلاف ، وعقد قلب على نفي ما تثبت ، أو إثبات ما تنفي .

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p249/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p249/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p249/r4.claim: Emphatic إن becomes especially apt when the assertion is unlikely or contrary to what people usually expect.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p249/r4.anchor: تراها تزداد حسنا إذا كان الخبر بأمر يبعد مثله في الظن ، وبشيء قد جرت عادة الناس بخلافه

DAMGHANI:v1p202/r14.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p202/r14.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p202/r14.claim: Arsala can mean to release people from punishment; Moses asks Pharaoh to release the Children of Israel, with parallels in al-Shuʿarāʾ and al-Aʿrāf.
DAMGHANI:v1p202/r14.anchor: أي أطلق من العذاب كقوله تعالى في سورة الشعراء

DAMGHANI:v1p202/r15.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p202/r15.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p202/r15.claim: The entry's seventh listed sense of arsala is to send down.
DAMGHANI:v1p202/r15.anchor: سلط بعث فتح أخرج وجه أطلق أنزل

SAMIN-DURR:20:47/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:47/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:20:47/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats the sign sentence as explaining the messengers' claim, which needs proof; the singular means a proof or miracle, though two signs were given, as in 7:105, 26:154, and 26:30.
SAMIN-DURR:20:47/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري: هذه الجملة جارية من الجملة الأولى وهي: { إنا رسولا ربك }

SAMIN-DURR:20:47/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:47/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:20:47/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says آية is singular because the purpose is to establish the claim with a proof, not to count the miracles.
SAMIN-DURR:20:47/r2.anchor: وإنما وحد ب " آية " ولم تثن ومعه آيتان؛ لأن المراد في هذا الموضع تثبيت الدعوى ببرهانها،

SAMIN-DURR:20:47/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:47/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:47/r3.claim: The greeting may be an instructed statement by the two messengers, then syntactically governed by فأتياه and فقولا, or an independent greeting with no syntactic position.
SAMIN-DURR:20:47/r3.anchor: و { على من اتبع الهدى } يحتمل أن يكون مأمورا بقوله: فيكون منصوب المحل كأنه قيل: فقولا أيضا: والسلام على من اتبع الهدى،

SAMIN-DURR:20:47/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:47/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:47/r4.claim: Some take على to mean ل, 'peace to whoever follows guidance'; the author says this recourse is unnecessary.
SAMIN-DURR:20:47/r4.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن " على " بمعنى اللام أي: والسلام لمن اتبع الهدى. وهذا لا حاجة إليه.

ASAD-NOTES:20:46#n30/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:46#n30/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:46#n30/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to Qur'anic parallels and Exodus i, 8–22 for a fuller description of Pharaoh's oppression of the Israelites.
ASAD-NOTES:20:46#n30/r1.anchor: For a more detailed description of this Pharaonic oppression of the Israelites, see Exodus i, 8-22.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r2.claim: Ta-Ha presents a joint mission: both are sent, answer in fear, receive reassurance, deliver the message, and are addressed by Pharaoh together, making Aaron Moses's partner in conveying the message.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r2.anchor: فقد أمر كلاً من موسى وهرون بالذهاب بآياته

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p690/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p690/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p690/r1.claim: The dual رسولَا in Ta-Ha fits its dual-centered context; the singular رسول in Shu'ara and Zukhruf fits their singular-centered passages, although Shu'ara begins with a dual address before shifting to singular.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p690/r1.anchor: المسألة تتعلق بالسياق ففي سورة طه السياق كله مبني على التثنية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p690/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p690/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p690/r2.claim: رسول can have singular or plural reference, like بشر, طفل, and ضيف; the author cites Quranic uses of those forms.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p690/r2.anchor: وكلمة (رسول) في اللغة تأتي مفرد وتأتي جمع مثل كلمة "بشر"

QIRAAT-ER:20:47:12#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:47:12#1/r1.speaker: HzT
QIRAAT-ER:20:47:12#1/r1.claim: The variant handles the hamza between rāʾ and yāʾ differently while preserving the full syllabic length of Isrāʾīl.
QIRAAT-ER:20:47:12#1/r1.anchor: Hamza-treatment variant — alternative handling of the hamza between rāʾ and yāʾ, preserving full syllabic length

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r1.claim: The command means to reach Pharaoh after being ordered to go, so it is not repetition; it coordinates with the preceding reassurance.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r1.anchor: أمر بإتيانه الذى هو عبارة عن الوصول إليه بعدما أمر بالذهاب إليه فلا تكرار

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r2.claim: They establish their mission at the outset so Pharaoh understands their standing; calling God their Lord is gentle, though Pharaoh may see it as belittling his claimed lordship.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r2.anchor: أمرا بذلك تحقيقا للحق من أول الأمر ليعرف الطاغية شأنهما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r3.claim: Release follows from their status as messengers; it means freeing Israel from captivity and abusive control, not ordering them to travel with Moses to Syria.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r3.anchor: ما بعدها على ما قبلها فان كونهما عليه السلام رسولي ربه تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r4.claim: Israel faced harsh digging, building, and stone-carrying labor; sons were killed in alternating years and women were put to service.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r4.anchor: فإنهم كانوا تحت ملكة القبط يستخدمونهم فى الأعمال الشاقة كالحفر والبناء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r5.claim: One explanation for beginning with release is gradual preaching: free the captives before changing Pharaoh’s belief.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r5.anchor: للتدريج فى الدعوة فإن إطلاق الأسرى دون تبديل الاعتقاد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r6.claim: Another view says freeing believers from unbelievers is more important; Alusi says this requires proof that Israel already believed in Moses or another prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r6.anchor: تخليص المؤمنين من الكفرة أهم من دعوتهم إلى الإيمان وهذا بعد تسليمه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r7.claim: A view says release clears an obstacle to Israel following Moses; Alusi objects that the context is calling Pharaoh and resisting his tyranny.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r7.anchor: لما فيه من إزالة المانع عن دعوتهم واتباعهم وهى أهم من دعوة القبط

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r8.claim: Another view says their first request was that Pharaoh believe, as indicated in al-Naziʿat; that request is omitted here because stated there, while release is omitted there because stated here.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r8.anchor: أول ما طلبا منه الأيمان كما ينبى عن ذلك آية النازعات

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r9.claim: This explanatory resumption confirms their prophetic claim and explains why Pharaoh must obey: the sign establishes their mission.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r9.anchor: استئناف بيانى وفيه تقرير لما تضمنه الكلام السابق من دعوى الرسالة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r10.claim: Repeating رب with Pharaoh addressed as its possessor reinforces the proof; قد marks certainty and emphasis, while construing it as expectation is strained.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r11.claim: The singular آية is used because the aim is one proof establishing their claim, not a count of separate proofs.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r11.anchor: وتوحيد الآية مع تعددها لأن المراد إثبات الدعوى ببرهانها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r12.claim: Some identify the sign specifically as Moses’ hand; Alusi dismisses this identification.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198/r13.claim: Others identify the sign specifically as the staff; Alusi dismisses this identification too.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#2/r1.claim: Here السلام means safety from punishment in both lives for those who follow guidance by affirming God’s signs; it is a verbal noun meaning safety, and على functions like لام.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#2/r1.anchor: السلامة من العذاب فى الدارين لمن اتبع ذلك بتصديق آيات الله تعالى الهادية الى الحق

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#2/r2.claim: Prepositions can exchange functions; على here also makes stylistic correspondence with the following العذاب على من كذب.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#2/r2.anchor: وعلى بمعنى اللام كما ورد عكسه فى قوله تعالى ( لهم اللعنة ) وحروف الجر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r2.speaker: الزمخشرى
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads السلام as the greeting of Paradise’s keepers to the guided, with the Fire’s keepers implicitly reproaching and warning deniers; this promises the Garden and suits the exhortation.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشرى : أي وسلام الملائكة الذين هم خزنة الجنة على المهتدين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r3.claim: Alusi calls al-Zamakhshari’s interpretation far from the apparent meaning; safety from punishment already gives full encouragement and warning in both lives.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r3.anchor: وانت تعلم أن هذا التفسير خلاف الظاهر جدا وانكار ذلك المكابرة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r4.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r4.claim: Al-Bahr calls al-Zamakhshari’s reading strange and says that taking punishment as for both lives and السلام as safety from it already fully encourages belief and warns against its opposite.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r4.anchor: وفي البحر هو تفسير غريب وانه إذا أريد من العذاب العذاب فى الدارين ومن السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan takes this as a closing greeting, السلام as salutation, addressed to the guided to encourage Pharaoh to join them.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r5.anchor: والسلام فيه بمعنى التحية وجاء ذلك على ما هو العادة من التسليم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan derives that Muslims should not greet unbelievers; if greeting is needed in speech or writing, use this formula.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r6.anchor: على منع السلام على الكفار وإذا احتيج اليه فى خطاب أو كتاب جئ بهذه الصيغة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r7.claim: Alusi cites the Prophet’s letter to Heraclius, beginning with سلام على من اتبع الهدى.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r7.anchor: ان رسول الله ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) كتب إلى هرقل من محمد رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r8.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r8.claim: Qatada says that when entering homes of People of the Book one should greet them with السلام على من اتبع الهدى.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r8.anchor: عن قتادة قال : التسليم على أهل الكتاب إذا دخلت عليهم بيوتهم أن تقول

ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r9.claim: The greeting reading is plausible only if their speech ended at السلام; since they continue with revelation, both sentences are best taken as dictated, the latter explaining the warning.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p198#3/r9.anchor: كلتا الجملتين من جملة المقول الملقن

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:47/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:47/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:47/r1.claim: The demand is that Pharaoh release the Israelites.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:47/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:47/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:47/r2.claim: Their mistreatment includes onerous labor and killing male children in alternating years while the Israelites were held by the Copts.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:47/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:47/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:47/r3.claim: Mentioning Israel's rescue immediately after arriving shows that saving believers from unbelievers is more important than calling unbelievers to faith; it may instead indicate gradual invitation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:47/r3.anchor: وتعقيب الإتيان بذلك دليل على أن تخليص المؤمنين من الكفرة أهم من دعوتهم إلى الإيمان

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:47/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:47/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:47/r4.claim: The singular sign confirms the claim to be messengers; it names proof of the claim rather than counting the signs, as do other passages that use singular sign or proof despite multiple miracles.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:47/r4.anchor: جملة مقررة لما تضمنه الكلام السابق من دعوى الرسالة

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:47/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:47/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:47/r5.claim: The greeting may be the angels' and keepers of Paradise's greeting to the rightly guided, or it may promise them safety in both abodes.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:47/r5.anchor: وسلام الملائكة وخزنة الجنة على المهتدين

BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r7.claim: God again emphasizes that they must go and speak to Pharaoh before giving them the words to say.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r8.claim: The emphatic dual wording signals their joint support; calling God Pharaoh’s Lord reduces Pharaoh to a servant and refutes his claim to divinity.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r8.anchor: ان فرعون ينكر ما تضمنه قولهما

BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r9.claim: They call God Pharaoh’s Lord because He raised and nurtured him after bringing him from nonexistence, showing Pharaoh is only one of His servants.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r9.anchor: إشارة إلى تحقيره بأنه من جملة عبيد مرسلها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r10.claim: They ask Pharaoh to release the Children of Israel so they can worship God, since no one else deserves worship.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r11.claim: They forbid Pharaoh to torment the Israelites through forced labor and slaughter.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r11.anchor: بما تعذبهم به من الاستخدام والتذبيح

BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r12.claim: The particle introducing their sign anticipates the audience’s expectation that a claim of messengership be supported with evidence.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p21/r12.anchor: مفتتحا بالحرف التوقع لأن حال السامع لادعاء الرسالة أن يتوقع دلالة على الإرسال

DURR-FULL:v5p580/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās transmits that the Prophet’s letter to Heraclius opened, “Peace upon whoever follows guidance.”
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r10.anchor: من طريق ابن عباس عن أبي سفيان بن حرب أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كتب إلى هرقل من محمد رسول الله إلى هرقل عظيم الروم سلام على من اتبع الهدى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r5.claim: إتيان means reaching and presenting themselves before Pharaoh; they are already near him in his city, so the instruction realizes the earlier command to go.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r6.claim: رسولا is dual in agreement with its two subjects; faʿūl with passive sense may either agree or remain unchanged, as in the cited Arabic examples and the singular form in 26:16.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r6.anchor: وجاءت تثنية رسول على الأصل في مطابقة الوصف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r7.claim: The request to release Israel follows as though already established, either because their purpose was known or because the request's importance makes it presumptive; God's messenger must be obeyed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r7.anchor: وأدخل فاء التفريع على طلب إطلاق بني إسرائيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r8.claim: Calling God your Lord presses the invitation on Pharaoh: if God is their Lord, He is all the more Lord of all people, despite Pharaoh's claim to divinity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r8.anchor: وخصا الرب بالإضافة إلى ضمير فرعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r9.claim: The requested end to torment concerns the forced, arduous labor imposed in service: Pharaoh treated Israelites as slaves and servants because they lived in his land.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p228/r9.anchor: والتعذيب الذي سألاه الكف عنه هو ما كان فرعون يسخر له بني إسرائيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p229/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p229/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p229/r1.claim: The sign statement explains their claim to be God's messengers and supports it with proof of divine sending; either purpose warrants separating the clause from the preceding one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p229/r1.anchor: وجملة { قد جئناك بآية من ربك } فيها بيان لجملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p229/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p229/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p229/r2.claim: They mention readiness to show a sign if Pharaoh wants one; belief without needing a miracle would be more complete. The sign was the staff becoming a serpent, followed by others.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p229/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p229/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p229/r3.claim: The request shows Moses' mission was to rescue Israel and establish an independent nation with a reforming law, not legislate for Egyptians; he still called Pharaoh's people to monotheism to oppose manifest wrongdoing and secure release.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p229/r3.anchor: والاقتصار على طلب إطلاق بني إسرائيل يدل على أن موسى أرسل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p229/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p229/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p229/r4.claim: السلام means safety and honor, not a greeting: no specific addressee is named, and greetings belong at an encounter's start, not mid-conversation; compare the Prophet's letter to Heraclius, أسلم تسلم.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p229/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p229/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p229/r5.claim: على implies established security for those who follow guidance; this precaution introduces the warning in 20:48 and indirectly invites Pharaoh to seek guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p229/r5.anchor: للتمكن ، أي سلامة من اتبع الهدى ثابتة لهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290#2/r1.claim: They ask Pharaoh to release the Israelites and stop torturing them; Pharaoh had put them to hard labor.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290#2/r1.anchor: أي خل عنهم ولا تعذبهم وكان يستعملهم في الأعمال الشاقة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies the sign from their Lord as the staff.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290#2/r3.claim: Muqatil says Moses displayed the transformed hand on one occasion and the staff on another.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290#2/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل أظهر اليد في مقام والعصا في مقام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290#2/r4.claim: Muqatil says those who follow guidance are those who believe in God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290#2/r4.anchor: قال مقاتل على من آمن بالله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says this is not a greeting; it means that followers of guidance are safe from God's punishment and anger, since it does not open an encounter.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p290#2/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج وليس يعني به التحية وإنما معناه أن من اتبع الهدى سلم من عذاب الله وسخطه والدليل على أنه ليس بسلام أنه ليس بابتداء لقاء وخطاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p296/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p296/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p296/r1.claim: In Ibn Abbas's hadith of al-Futun, Moses and Aaron waited at Pharaoh's door for a time without permission, then were admitted after a severe barrier was lifted.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p296/r1.anchor: قد تقدم في حديث "الفتون" عن ابن عباس أنه قال: مكثا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p296/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p296/r2.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق بن يسار
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p296/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the brothers waited at the palace for two years, with no one daring to inform Pharaoh, until a court entertainer told him; Pharaoh summoned them, and Moses identified himself as a messenger whom Pharaoh recognized.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p296/r2.anchor: وذكر محمد بن إسحاق بن يسار: أن موسى وأخاه هارون خرجا، فوقفا بباب فرعون يلتمسان الإذن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p296/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p296/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p296/r3.claim: Al-Suddi relates that Moses reunited with his mother and brother, enlisted Aaron to help summon Pharaoh, and they went by night; after Moses knocked with his staff, guards called him mad, but Pharaoh ordered them in.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p296/r3.anchor: وذكر السدي أنه لما قدم بلاد مصر، ضاف أمه وأخاه وهما لا يعرفانه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297/r1.claim: The “sign” is a proof and miracle from God; “peace upon whoever follows guidance” means peace to Pharaoh if he follows guidance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297/r1.anchor: وقوله: {قد جئناك بآية من ربك} أي: بدلالة ومعجزة من ربك، {والسلام على من اتبع الهدى} أي: والسلام عليك إن اتبعت الهدى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297/r2.claim: The Prophet opened his letter to Heraclius with the same greeting, then invited him to Islam and promised safety and a doubled reward from God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297/r2.anchor: ولهذا لما كتب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى هرقل عظيم الروم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297/r3.claim: Musaylimah claimed partnership in prophethood and divided the land and its people between them; Muhammad answered him with the same greeting and God's promise to grant the land to whichever servants He wills.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297/r3.anchor: وكذلك لما كتب مسيلمة إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كتابا صورته

JISHUMI:v7p4674/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r1.claim: Salām for those following guidance means safety for both worlds through the truth brought by the messengers; the next warning says punishment awaits those who deny messengers and turn from truth.
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r1.anchor: ثم بينا أن سلامة الدارين لمن اتبعهما، فقال سبحانه: والسلام على من اتبع الهدى أي: الحق الذي جئنا به

JISHUMI:v7p4674/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r2.claim: The messengers' command and prohibition are joined to promise and threat.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r4.claim: Pharaoh and the Copts held the Israelites in bondage, imposing digging, construction, carrying stones, and other forced labor, while killing their sons and enslaving their women.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r4.anchor: كانت بنو إسرائيل في ملكة فرعون والقبط ، يعذبونهم بتكليف الأعمال الصعبة : من الحفر والبناء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r5.claim: The statement about bringing a sign explains the claim to be the Lord’s messengers, since the claimed mission requires its proof.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r5.anchor: جملة جارية من الجملة الأولى وهي { إنا رسولا ربك } مجرى البيان والتفسير ، لأن دعوى الرسالة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r6.claim: The singular “a sign” is generic proof of their claim even though they brought two miracles.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r6.anchor: ولم يثن ومعه آيتان : لأن المراد في هذا الموضع تثبيت الدعوى ببرهانها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r7.claim: The greeting is the angels, guardians of Paradise, welcoming those who follow guidance, while Hell’s guardians rebuke the deniers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p67#2/r7.anchor: يريد : وسلام الملائكة الذين هم خزنة الجنة على المهتدين

MUQATIL:20:46-47/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:46-47/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:46-47/r4.claim: God's speech to Moses ends here; when the brothers reach Pharaoh, Moses tells him to send the Israelites with them and not enslave them through forced labor.
MUQATIL:20:46-47/r4.anchor: فانقطع كلام الله عز وجل لموسى، عليه السلام، فلما أتيا فرعون

MUQATIL:20:46-47/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:46-47/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:46-47/r5.claim: With us means Moses and Aaron, and not torment them means not subjecting the Israelites to forced labor.
MUQATIL:20:46-47/r5.anchor: فأرسل معنا بني إسرائيل ولا تعذبهم

MUQATIL:20:46-47/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:46-47/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:46-47/r6.claim: The sign from God is a token, namely the hand and the staff.
MUQATIL:20:46-47/r6.anchor: يعني بعلامة { من ربك } وهي اليد والعصا

MUQATIL:20:46-47/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:46-47/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:46-47/r7.claim: Peace is upon whoever follows guidance by believing in God.
MUQATIL:20:46-47/r7.anchor: والسلام على من اتبع الهدى } [آية: 47] يقول: والسلام على من آمن بالله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#4/r1.claim: The person they approach is Pharaoh.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#4/r2.claim: They ask Pharaoh to release Israelites from enslavement and forced labor.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#4/r2.anchor: ﴿ فأرسل معنا بني إسرائيل ﴾ أي اطلقهم على الاستبعاد والاسترقاق ﴿ ولا تعذبهم ﴾ بتكليف المشاق

NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#4/r3.claim: The sign is proof of their messengership; the clause explains the claim, which can only be established by signs.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#4/r3.anchor: بحجة على صدق ما ادعيناه وهذه الجملة جارية من الجملة الاولى وهي أنا رسولا ربك مجرى البيان والتفسير والتفصيل لأن دعوى الرسالة لا تثبت إلا ببينتا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#4/r4.claim: When Pharaoh asked what the sign was, Moses showed his hand shining like sunlight.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#4/r4.anchor: فقال فرعون وما هي فاخرج يده لها شعاع كشعاع الشمس

NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#4/r5.claim: Whoever submits is safe from punishment; this is not a greeting, though another view makes it angels' greeting to the guided in Paradise.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56#4/r5.anchor: أي سلم من العذاب من أسلم وليس بتحية وقيل وسلام الملائكة الذين هم خزنة الجنة على المهتدين

BURSEVI:v5p301/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p301/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p301/r1.claim: Coming to Pharaoh is not redundant with the prior command to go: coming implies easy arrival, whereas coming more generally considers reaching; either can describe intending to arrive.
BURSEVI:v5p301/r1.anchor: {فأتياه} أمرا بإتيانه الذي هو عبارة عن الوصول إليه بعدما أمرا بالذهاب

BURSEVI:v5p301/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p301/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p301/r2.claim: They are to state their message from the outset so the tyrant understands their claim and frames his reply accordingly.
BURSEVI:v5p301/r2.anchor: {فقولا} من أول الأمر {إنا رسولا ربك} ليعرف الطاغي

BURSEVI:v5p301/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p301/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p301/r3.claim: Rasūl is the dual of rasūl, a rare faʿūl form meaning one who bears a message; conventionally it can be human or angel sent to convey rulings, while nabī is restricted to a human.
BURSEVI:v5p301/r3.anchor: ورسولا تثنية رسول وهو فعول مبالغة مفعل بضم الميم وفتح العين

BURSEVI:v5p301/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p301/r4.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v5p301/r4.claim: Al-Baḥr explains the request as releasing the Israelites and letting them go with Moses and Aaron to Palestine, their ancestral home; Palestine lies between Syria and Egypt and includes Ramla, Gaza, and Ascalon.
BURSEVI:v5p301/r4.anchor: ما قال في "بحر العلوم" فأطلقهم وخلهم يذهبوا معنا إلى فلسطين

BURSEVI:v5p301/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p301/r5.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v5p301/r5.claim: Al-Irshād takes sending to mean freeing the Israelites from captivity and oppressive control, not requiring them to travel to Syria; the prohibition on torment supports this reading.
BURSEVI:v5p301/r5.anchor: وقال في "الإرشاد" بالإرسال إطلاقهم من الأسر والقسر وإخراجهم

BURSEVI:v5p301/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p301/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p301/r6.claim: The Israelites were subjected to hard labor such as digging and carrying stones, their sons were killed every other year, and their women were made servants.
BURSEVI:v5p301/r6.anchor: فإنهم كانوا تحت مملكة القبط يستخدمونهم في الأعمال الصعبة الفادحة

BURSEVI:v5p301/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p301/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p301/r7.claim: Placing the demand to release believers between the claim of messengership and the promised sign stresses that rescuing believers from unbelievers matters more than merely inviting them to faith.
BURSEVI:v5p301/r7.anchor: وتوسيط حكم الإرسال بين رسالتهما وبين ذكر المجيء بآية دالة

BURSEVI:v5p301/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p301/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p301/r8.claim: ʿAdhāb means severe pain or affliction. Its proposed origins include making someone hungry and sleepless, removing life's sweetness, or repeatedly striking with the tip of a whip.
BURSEVI:v5p301/r8.anchor: والعذاب هو الإيجاء الشديد وقد عذبه تعذيبا أي : أكثر حبسه

BURSEVI:v5p301#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p301#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p301#2/r1.claim: The sign is singular despite multiple miracles because the point is to establish their claim with proof, not enumerate the proofs.
BURSEVI:v5p301#2/r1.anchor: وتوحيد الآية مع تعددها لأن المراد إثبات الدعوى ببرهانها

BURSEVI:v5p301#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p301#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p301#2/r2.claim: The definite article in al-salām identifies peace as a general kind; the expression can be read as a greeting whose implied blessing brings safety in both abodes.
BURSEVI:v5p301#2/r2.anchor: {والسلام} اللام لتعريف الماهية والسلامة التعري من الآفات

BURSEVI:v5p301#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p301#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p301#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, al-salām means safety and ʿalā functions like li, as in the reverse prepositional usage in the statement that they have the curse.
BURSEVI:v5p301#2/r3.anchor: وأما السلامة فعلى بمعنى اللام كعكسه في قوله تعالى : {ولهم اللعنة}

BURSEVI:v5p301#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p301#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p301#2/r4.claim: Following guidance means affirming God's truth-guiding signs, whether physically or by conforming and obeying; the latter sense also appears in the verse promising no fear to those who follow God's guidance.
BURSEVI:v5p301#2/r4.anchor: بتصديق آيات الله الهادية إلى الحق فاللام على أصلها كما في سلام عليكم

BURSEVI:v5p301#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p301#2/r5.speaker: التأويلات
BURSEVI:v5p301#2/r5.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt says whoever submits and follows God's guidance brought by His prophets is safe.
BURSEVI:v5p301#2/r5.anchor: قال في "التأويلات" : سلم من استسلم واتبع هدى الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r12.claim: The command to go is reiterated through four stages: to show Moses the great signs, to send Moses and Aaron, to go to Pharaoh, and now to approach him with the message.
RAZI-FULL:v22p53/r12.anchor: أعاد ذلك التكليف فقال : { فأتياه } لأنه سبحانه وتعالى قال في المرة الأولى : { لنريك من ءاياتنا الكبرى * اذهب إلى فرعون }

RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r1.claim: The first demand is severe because it requires Pharaoh, the ruling king, to submit to the messengers’ authority.
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r1.anchor: انقياده إليهما والتزامه لطاعتهما وذلك يعظم على الملك المتبوع

RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r2.claim: Demanding Israel’s release diminishes Pharaoh’s sovereignty because he depends on their labor for construction and other work.
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r2.anchor: قوله : { فأرسل معنا بنى إسراءيل } فيه إدخال النقص على ملكه لأنه كان محتاجا إليهم فيما يريده من الأعمال

RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r3.claim: The prohibition against abusing the Israelites is another element that makes the message more forceful.

RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r4.claim: Claiming to have brought a sign from Pharaoh’s Lord adds a fourth forceful assertion to the message.
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r4.anchor: قوله : { قد جئناك بئاية من ربك }

RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r5.claim: Gentleness comes first, then firmness once the hearer’s obstinacy appears.
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r5.anchor: لأن الإنسان إذا ظهر لجاجه فلا بد له من التغليظ

RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r6.claim: It is better to state the set of demands first and then prove that whole set by the miracle, rather than mention the miracle before the requests.
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r6.anchor: بل هذا أولى من تأخيره عنه لأنهم ذكروا مجموع الدعاوى ثم استدلوا على ذلك المجموع بالمعجزة

RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r7.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r7.claim: Al-Qaffāl explains the singular “sign” generically: it can denote one proof or several proofs.
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r7.anchor: أجاب القفال بأن معنى الآية الإشارة إلى جنس الآيات كأنه قال : قد جئناك ببيان من عند الله ثم يجوز أن يكون ذلك حجة واحدة أو حججا كثيرة

RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r8.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r8.claim: One view takes the greeting of peace as God’s command to Moses and Aaron to say it to Pharaoh.
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r8.anchor: فقال بعضهم هو من قول الله تعالى لهما

RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r9.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r9.claim: Another view ends God’s speech at “a sign from your Lord” and treats the greeting as Moses and Aaron’s promise of safety in this life and the next to believers.
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r9.anchor: وقال آخرون بل كلام الله تعالى قد تم عند قوله

RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r10.claim: Here salām means safety, as in the related noun forms riḍāʿ and riḍāʿa.
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r10.anchor: والسلام بمعنى السلامة كما يقال رضاع ورضاعة

RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r11.claim: The preposition ʿalā can function like li, as in verses saying curse or harm is “for” people.
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r11.anchor: واللام وعلى ههنا بمعنى واحد كما قال

RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r14.claim: A second proof is that everyone who follows guidance is promised safety; the knower of God follows guidance and therefore is safe.
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r14.anchor: وقد فسرنا السلام بالسلامة فظاهره يقتضي حصول السلامة
